_about: Hand-set design controls the solvers must honour (docs/roadway_control_plan.md §8). horizontal: per route, pinned PIs and radii ('pis': [[x, z], ...], 'radii': one per PI, 'note', optional 'sta': [from, to] metres along the route's OSM line to pin only that stretch): build_alignments.py uses them instead of the fit, and they are authoritative downstream (horizontal_overrides.py); Bridge Composer's Alignments mode writes them. profile: per route (alignments.json id), 'ignore_ground': [[from_sta, to_sta], ...] leaves DEM samples there out of the vertical fit; 'pins': [{'sta': m, 'elevation': game Y of the top of pavement, 'grade': fraction (optional)}] are fixed controls; 'pvi_stations': [m, ...] fixes the route's PVI stations (the ends are added; each curve is as long as its shorter straight, and refinement leaves the route alone). Stations are the route's, metres from its 0+00. templates: per route and station range, cross-section fields that replace the template's (templates.py OVERRIDE_KEYS: curb_to_curb_ft/m, lanes, parking, section, sidewalk_m, ...), each with its 'note'; entries with source 'building_faces' are derived, and rewritten, by templates.py --faces.

profile.note: Downtown service alley at (1824, -1428): its mapped west end runs 6 m past the top of a 4 m wall or pad edge in the DEM (ground +42%). The alley is held at the terrace grade to its mapped end instead of diving off the wall.

Service drive at (850, -1855) crossing the abandoned IC rail embankment: the ground rises 6.5 m in 20 m and falls 6 m in 15 m (a 68% grade change in 10 m at its crest). Graded as a drive over a berm would be, a 14 m crest curve over the berm and a sag that runs out 13 m before Chuck Vail Drive, so the drive meets it on a straight; up to about 1.15 m comes off the crest. The OSM rail crosses 12 m east of the DEM's crest and is drawn 1.4 m off the ground there, so its top of rail is taken from the ground (build_profiles RAIL_TRUST_M).
